name: Twenty One Pilots
description: The self-released debut from Columbus, Ohio. Piano-driven, raw and introspective, it's where the story begins.
story: Released independently on 29 December 2009, the self-titled debut shows twenty one pilots before they became a duo. It is the only album with founding members Nick Thomas and Chris Salih, who both left the band in 2011.

It is a raw, home-grown record from Columbus, Ohio, with piano and introspective writing at its centre. Many of the themes that run through the band's later work, like doubt, faith and mental health, are already here.

name: Vessel
description: Their first major-label album. Clean, quiet greys, with the band's grandfathers on the cover.
story: Released on 8 January 2013, Vessel was the band's third studio album and their first on Fueled by Ramen: their major-label debut. It entered the Billboard 200 at number 58, but kept growing and peaked at number 21 in 2016, after the band's mainstream breakthrough.

Its success came slowly but lasted. By July 2019 it had passed two million equivalent units in the US, and every track was certified at least Gold, making twenty one pilots the first act to achieve this with two separate albums.

name: Blurryface
description: Named after a character who stands for insecurity. Red and black, with painted hands and necks.
story: Released on 17 May 2015, Blurryface is named after a character who embodies the narrator's insecurities. The album deals with mental health, doubt and faith, and gave the band two hit singles, "Stressed Out" and "Ride", both top five on the US Billboard Hot 100.

It was their breakthrough and their first number one on the Billboard 200. In 2018 it became the first album of the digital era with every track certified at least Gold, and by May 2019 it had spent four straight years on the Billboard 200 without ever leaving the chart.

name: Trench
description: A concept album about escaping the walled city of Dema. Yellow tape, vultures and Banditos.
story: After a year of public silence, the band returned on 5 October 2018 with Trench, recorded in secret. It is a concept album set around Dema, a walled city, and the land around it called Trench, using that world to talk about mental health and doubt.

Singles like "Jumpsuit", "Nico and the Niners", "Levitate" and "My Blood" came first, followed by the Bandito Tour. Critics praised its ambition and cohesive sound, Rock Sound named it the best album of 2018, and it reached number one in six countries.

name: Scaled And Icy
description: Bright and pastel on the surface, written during lockdown. Blue dragons on a pink sky.
story: Released on 21 May 2021, Scaled and Icy was made during the COVID-19 pandemic. Its title plays on "scaled back and isolated", the way Tyler Joseph described music made in that period.

Under its bright, colourful surface there is a clue: the title is an anagram of "Clancy is dead", pointing back to the protagonist of Trench. A livestream edition followed in November 2021, with tracks from the band's online "Livestream Experience".

name: Clancy
description: The return to Dema's storyline, told from Clancy's point of view. Fire red and yellow.
story: Released on 24 May 2024, Clancy is named after the protagonist first introduced in Trench. It is a visual album and the first of two records that close the conceptual story the band began with Blurryface in 2015.

Written by Tyler Joseph and produced with long-time collaborator Paul Meany, it was announced on 29 February 2024 after weeks of fan speculation. It reached number one in Australia, Germany and Scotland, and the Clancy World Tour ran from August 2024 to October 2025.

name: Breach
description: The latest chapter. Dark rooms lit by a red glow, picking up where Clancy left off.
story: Released on 12 September 2025, Breach follows Clancy and brings the conceptual series to an end, closing the story told across Blurryface, Trench, Scaled and Icy and Clancy.

Mainly written by Tyler Joseph and co-produced with Paul Meany and Mike Elizondo, it became the band's second album to debut at number one on the Billboard 200, with the biggest opening-week vinyl sales for a rock album since tracking began in 1991.
